sections.h2: The above-₹10,000 price band has the best Sharpe ratio of the five bands

chart.title: The above-₹10,000 band ranks first on Sharpe ratio; under-₹1,000 ranks last
chart.sub: Sharpe ratio, 3.5 years of weekly prices, 6.5% risk-free proxy.
chart.source: This post's price-band simulation, January 2023 to August 2026.

sections.means: Ranking the five bands by Sharpe ratio puts the highest-priced stocks first, a lead the post traces to a 44.4% return rather than lower risk.
sections.todo: Do not choose a price band on the strength of this ranking, because the post finds price is not a recognised risk factor.

sections.h2: The under-₹1,000 portfolio has the highest volatility, at 22.4%

chart.title: Under-₹1,000 volatility of 22.4% sits well above the other four bands' 16.1–17.3%
chart.source: This post's price-band simulation, January 2023 to August 2026.

sections.means: The cheapest band pairs the highest volatility with the lowest return, 19.0%, which is why its Sharpe ratio is the weakest.
sections.todo: Weigh a large number of holdings against the filter behind them, since 1,987 stocks did not fix the weaker risk-return profile.

sections.h2: Simulated bands score above published fund Sharpe ratios, with caveats

chart.title: Published fund Sharpe ratios of 0.88 to 1.18 sit below every band except under-₹1,000

chart.source: Secondary sources cited in this post; this post's price-band simulation.

sections.means: The post warns the comparison is not like-for-like, because real funds pay expense ratios and use rolling windows the simulation does not.
